title: ContextSafe event log summary 0.1
$comment: What `contextsafe events summarize` derives from one local event log: the number of records, the number of each command, of each outcome, and of each error code, and the SHA-256 of the bytes read. It is derived, deterministic, and unsigned. It carries counts, closed values, and one digest only: no timestamp, no path, no free text, and nothing from any input a logged command read. `counts_by_command` names every command the log's record vocabulary publishes, so a command added to that vocabulary moves this contract's version.
x-contextsafe-semantic-constraints: every key of counts_by_command is present, including the commands the log holds no record of, so the shape does not change with the log's contents
counts_by_error_code holds only codes the log actually carries, because the set of error codes is open where the set of commands is closed
record_count is the number of records read and equals the sum of counts_by_command and the sum of counts_by_outcome

log_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact bytes read, which is the empty-string digest for a log holding no record; it is not a chain, and a log cut back to an earlier line summarises as a valid shorter log
a log line that is not one canonical record refuses the whole summary; a summary is never derived from the lines that happened to parse
